paper_id: Li et al. - 2014 - Towards Energy-Fairness in Asynchronous Duty-Cycling Sensor Networks
title: Towards Energy-Fairness in Asynchronous Duty-Cycling Sensor Networks
motivation: Sensor nodes powered by batteries; frequent replacements prohibited; gap between limited energy and long-term deployment needs.
problem_framing: Sleep Interval Control (SIC) problem formulated as convex optimization minimizing maximum energy consumption rate (min-max fairness).
key_insight: SIC is convex, enabling decomposition into local sub-problems solvable in a distributed manner while achieving global optimum.
method_signature: GDSIC: distributed convex optimization via local information exchange among sensor nodes.
evaluation_criteria: Maximum energy consumption rate minimization; network lifetime extension; convergence speed and scalability.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Greedy SIC strategy leads network to suboptimal value far above optimal result (4.9 vs 2.8 mJ/s in case study).
evidence_for_taste: greedy strategy is not always effective
